study type: Quasi-experimental (Difference-in-Difference) study using repeated cross-sectional survey data, coupled with a cost-benefit analysis
cohort: Participants were births captured in the 2014 Demographic Health Survey in Kenya, specifically comparing those occurring before and after the Free Maternity Policy implementation in June 2013.
finding: The Kenyan Free Maternity Policy significantly reduced the probabilities of early neonatal mortality by 17-21% and neonatal mortality by 19-20%, demonstrating a positive net social benefit.
mod_finding: The probability of birth happening through Caesarean Section reduced by 1.7% after implementing the FMP, though this finding was not statistically significant.
followup_time: Up to 28 days after birth (neonatal period)
cross-section timing: Data was collected from the 2014 Demographic Health Survey, comparing births before and after the June 2013 policy implementation.
